speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We also have an active AI industry research scene, with industry research and development (R&D) centres by companies, such as Salesforce, SAP and Alibaba.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: For example, Singapore has built up thriving aerospace manufacturing and aviation services without developing or owning aircraft technologies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: That said, we recognise the value of investing in research capabilities to support talent development and enterprise innovation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We have a vibrant research ecosystem for AI and will continue to support useful endeavours, including various aspects of FMs.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Could I just clarify then that there is no whole-of-Government plan to develop indigenous AI FMs in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I am asking this because many other countries, including the United Kingdom, Japan, Korea, even Saudi Arabia and the UAE, are committing to ambitious programmes to develop their own indigenous FMs.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: On the other hand, Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said last month, during his trip to the United States that Singapore is not at the cutting edge of ITS.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The latest ideas and innovations will still come from American universities and companies, but that we can be a fast adopter.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: So, can I clarify that the approach for Singapore is that we are going to be a fast adopter and not going to lead in the building of FMs?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And lastly, when using the large language models (LLMs) developed by foreign companies, how does it ensure that the confidential data is not disclosed?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: On the last question that Mr Gerald Giam has asked, it is large area about how we protect the privacy of our systems and the management of data around AI.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I would encourage them to file a question on that so that we could have a discussion.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I would say though that I would push back a little and disagree with his characterisations that we are either going to outsource or we are going to develop capabilities locally.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And most use cases in the world leverage on existing FMs, either off-the-shelf, customise via methods, such as retrieval augmentation of finetuning.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We do have groups that are experimenting and building FMs on such issues, such as to better translate regional languages, improving our understanding on how to govern FMs.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: They are open for public and research use and we have received industry interest.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The Government also has been proactively looking at how to develop FMs to improve our own productivity.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
